previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and recent pneumonia was readmitted for right-sided pleuritic chest and back pain, diarrhea, and headache. She had recently completed a course of levofloxacin, which she stopped due to nausea and diarrhea. Evaluation revealed no pulmonary embolus or active infection on CT chest, with findings suggesting musculoskeletal or post-viral pain. Diarrhea resolved spontaneously, attributed to antibiotic use. Hyperglycemia was noted, with A1C pending. Anxiety, related to pain and prior psychiatric history, improved during admission. She was discharged home on tramadol for pain, with continuation of lithium and Thorazine, and instructed to follow up with her PCP and mental health provider.

medications were not restarted and she was monitored on 
telemetry.  Her QT interval improved on ___ and was WNL.  Her 
lytes were repleted.

with clonidine, haldol and olanzapine. This resolved overnight
